resources.string: Blocks touches from a damaged part of the screen and gives you a trackpad and an on-screen cursor to drive the phone with instead.
1. Allow drawing over other apps, so the blocker, cursor and trackpad can sit above whatever you are using.
2. Turn on the Mouse accessibility service, so the cursor can actually tap things. Find it under Settings › Accessibility › Mouse.
The bubble follows your finger and the cursor moves with it. Let go and the bubble slides back to its spot, while the cursor stays where you left it, so you can cross the screen in several strokes.

Slide to move the cursor — lifting your finger does not tap. Tap without sliding to click where the cursor is. Double tap and release to long press. Double tap and, without lifting, slide to drag: slide straight away to scroll, or rest a moment first to pick something up.\n\nThe blocked area is only outlined while this screen is open, so nothing marks your screen while you use the phone.
